morphology.habit: Annual, rarely perennial, 15–80 cm; woody taprooted caudex
morphology.stems: Erect, few branches at mid/distal nodes, sparsely pilose
morphology.leaves: Alternate; basal 30–60 × 3–8 mm, often withered; stem leaves narrow, hispid/pilose, sometimes stipitate-glandular
morphology.rays: (7–)10(–14) fertile pistillate yellow rays, blades 6–13 × 1–2 mm
morphology.fruits: Ray cypselae triangular in section and densely strigose; pappus 2–3 series with bristles outer 1–2.5 mm and inner 2–3 mm
morphology.habitat: Open sandy/gravelly soils, pine-oak-juniper woods, roadsides

unresolved_notes: 1999 regional flora treated this under Chrysopsis texana, p.336; FNA treats it as Bradburia hirtella.
Existing species card lacks morphology_keys; do not replace original content.

morphology.habit: Shrub with woody branched stems, ~60–120 cm (existing source-backed species record)
morphology.leaves: Alternate, short-petiolate 1–2 mm, lanceolate to lance-ovate 5–40 × 3.5–12 mm; teeth variable
morphology.heads: Narrow paniculiform group of disk-only heads
morphology.fruits: Cypselae ca. 3.5–4 mm, usually glabrous; pappus 30–35 tawny bristles

unresolved_notes: No matching regional-flora species paragraph confirmed; morphology quoted from existing carefully researched species record and flagged for secondary-source recheck.

morphology.leaves: Opposite, petioled; ovate to ovate-lanceolate or deltoid, 1–3(–4) cm, toothed
morphology.heads: Small solitary heads on short axillary peduncles
morphology.fruits: Pappus two awns, sometimes 1–3 additional rudimentary awns
morphology.habitat: Lawn weed or deliberately planted shady cover

unresolved_notes: Regional source says April–July; do not generalize year-round flowering from other geographic treatments.

morphology.leaves: Alternate, sometimes nearly opposite above, elliptic to ovate/oblong, usually simple with few spine teeth
morphology.heads: Terminal, phyllaries spine-tipped, outer phyllaries leafy and spreading
morphology.disc: Bright orange to yellow-orange tubular florets
morphology.fruits: Ivory white glabrous achenes ~6 × 4 mm, pappus normally absent, rarely rudimentary/well-developed bristle scales

unresolved_notes: Regional flora reports very limited Texas collections as of 1999; don't translate to present-day frequency.

morphology.leaves: Alternate; lower oblanceolate and toothed/lobed; upper narrow oblanceolate, often white-woolly beneath, decurrent onto stem
morphology.heads: Centaurea: terminal solitary/corymbose, no true ray florets, outer disk florets enlarged to resemble rays
morphology.phyllaries: Margins with many tiny often dark teeth, without terminal sharp spines
morphology.disc: Blue, purple, pink or white; outer sterile showy florets

unresolved_notes: Do not describe outer enlarged florets as true ray florets.

morphology.leaves: Lower pinnately lobed with rounded lobes; upper linear, decurrent onto stems
morphology.heads: Small heads, involucres about 1 cm excluding spines
morphology.phyllaries: Terminal sharp spine 3–9 mm, often darker than body
morphology.rays: Absent, outer disk florets may appear radiate per genus

unresolved_notes: Phenology is absent from source's species paragraph; do not invent season.
European origin documented in 1999 flora; keep separated from BONAP county evidence.

morphology.fruits: Minute thickened pappus ring distinguishing from C. effusa's perennial rootstock and tiny erose crown

morphology.leaves: Alternate, flat; proximal stem blades oblong to lanceolate-oblong, 6–12 mm wide, bases truncate to subcordate; distal leaves reduced
morphology.heads: Solitary terminal radiate with pale rays and yellow discs per genus
morphology.fruits: Pappus minute erose crown or thickened ring <0.1 mm

unresolved_notes: Separate from taprooted annual C. bellidifolia; both may have tiny pappus.

morphology.habit: Tufted perennial, 10–15(–20) cm, forming patches from creeping roots; FNA key notes short stems 6–12 cm
morphology.leaves: Alternate, crowded, narrow oblanceolate, 2–12(–15) mm long, ≤2 mm wide, entire, firm; FNA notes strong raised midrib and longitudinal grooves above
morphology.heads: Solitary terminal heads on numerous branches; involucres 5–7 mm high
morphology.rays: White to rosy with age, 2–3 mm; curl under at night/age
morphology.fruits: Achenes 2–3 mm; FNA: 1 series of (20–)24–26(–30) barbellate pappus bristles

unresolved_notes: 1999 flora lists Aster arenosus and Leucelene ericoides as synonyms.
FNA key separates it from other Chaetopappa using densely overlapping grooved leaves and true bristle pappus.

morphology.leaves: Oblanceolate to obovate-lyrate, 6–15 × 2.4–4 cm, underside conspicuously white-tomentose
morphology.stems: Leafless peduncles 10–60 cm, sometimes 1–2 tiny bracts
morphology.heads: Solitary, nodding in flower but erect in fruit, roughly 150 flowers
morphology.phyllaries: White-tomentose, tips often dark and nearly glabrous
morphology.florets: Peripheral pistillate ray-like cream turning crimson; inner pistillate filiform; central perfect
morphology.fruits: Achenes 9–16 mm including a filiform beak making up about 2/3 of length; pappus buff-white bristles 13–14 mm

unresolved_notes: 1999 synonym Chaptalia nutans var. texana; verify modern placement before making taxonomy edits.
